title: Star trails over the ESO 3.6-meter telescope
caption: Star trails over the ESO 3.6-meter telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars trace long arcs across the sky above the ESO 3.6-meter telescope in this photograph. The trails form because the camera's shutter stays open while the Earth turns, so each star draws a curved line rather than appearing as a point.

Beneath them, the telescope is home to HARPS (the High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher), which ESO describes as the world's foremost exoplanet hunter. Instead of taking pictures of planets, instruments like HARPS look for the tiny back-and-forth wobble a planet causes in its star as the two orbit each other.

This image was shared through the Your ESO Pictures Flickr Group, a place where anyone can submit photos connected with ESO. That openness lets many different photographers share their own views of ESO's telescopes under the night sky.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken at ESO's La Silla Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only a long exposure turns the Earth's rotation into visible trails.
